    "design_critique": "1. The revision changes four controller values at once (kp 3.5 to 4.0, kd 0.15 to 0.3, ki 0.05 to 0.5, base_speed 1.5 to 1.4). The rationale says it is testing one hypothesis, the mismatch offset, but the next race cannot attribute a result to ki alone. A better test would change ki by itself, or pair it only with the speed change the decision rule requires.

2. The offset explanation does not match the failure location. A fixed left/right mismatch makes lateral drift grow with time. In iteration 0 every run left the track at progress 0.105 to 0.148 (roughly 0.3 to 0.5 m, or 0.3 to 0.5 s), and this holds on all three tracks, which have different shapes. A common early failure point points to a start transient, a first-bend turn-in, or the initial line acquisition, not a slow accumulating bias. The revision does not address why all three tracks fail at about the same progress.

3. The rms argument is misframed. The rationale says rms_error of 0.025 to 0.031 is 'well above the 0.0125 m half-width'. The half-width is not the failure limit. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03), which is 0.06 m. Those rms values are averages over short runs that end when the robot exits, so they show the robot was already drifting, not that it sat at a steady offset for long. The offset diagnosis should rest on the timing of error growth, not on comparing rms with the tape half-width.

4. The integral term is not a clean offset estimator. On a curve the signal is non-zero for the whole bend, so the integral accumulates the bend's own signal, and it is not reset when the bend ends. On the oval, where turns are mostly one direction, ki=0.5 can build up to 1.0 turn units (about 350 PWM per wheel) in the direction of the curve. That is a real steering bias that could push the robot off the outside edge on a long bend. The rationale says ki is 'inert only for small ki' but does not check whether a large ki pushes the robot off the track on the curved tracks. The integral units (per step or per second) are also not stated, so the 1.0 turn-unit figure cannot be verified.

5. The speed cut runs against the stated goal. The rationale itself says completion needs about 1.5 m/s average, and the 3 s limit enforces it. A 1.4 base_speed, which is 6.7% lower PWM, makes finishing harder. Nothing in the race data shows speed is the cause of the early exit. The cut is justified by the decision rule, but that rule was written for the case where max_error exceeds 0.05, and the same rule would also fire for the legitimate line recovery the previous critique flagged.

6. kp and ki are raised together with no stability check. A higher ki adds phase lag on top of kp 4.0 and kd 0.3, and the steering_oscillation figures (0.10 to 0.14) do not show how much margin is left. The rationale does not say how far kp can rise before oscillation grows.

7. Geometry is unchanged and this is still a reasonable choice. The sensor spacing of 0.02 m covers offsets up to about 0.04 m, and at the outermost sensors (x = plus or minus 0.04) the footprint still sees tape for lateral offsets up to about 0.0585 m, almost the off-track limit. That leaves little room for line-loss recovery at the outer edge.

8. The line-loss recovery (last_direction) is untested and was not reconsidered. It is the mechanism that fires when the line is lost, which happened about once per run, so it is part of the failure mode and not a secondary detail.",
